t: Ashikaga Takauji set up his military government in Kyoto in 1336 after overthrowing the Kenmu Restoration of Emperor Go-Daigo.
It was the weakest of Japan's three military governments, depending on the loyalty of the daimyō because the shōgun held little territory of his own.
Oda Nobunaga drove the fifteenth shōgun, Ashikaga Yoshiaki, out of Kyoto in 1573, ending the shogunate.
dyk: The name Muromachi comes from the Muromachi district of Kyoto, where the third shōgun, Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, built his residence known as the "Flower Palace" in 1379.
ev: Ashikaga Takauji establishes his own military government in Kyoto, overthrowing the Kenmu Restoration
Ashikaga Yoshimitsu establishes the "Flower Palace" on Muromachi Street in Kyoto
The Southern Court gives up and the Northern and Southern Courts are combined into one
The death of Ashikaga Yoshinori leaves the authority of the bakufu almost vanished
The Ōnin War breaks out among the daimyō, beginning the Sengoku period
The shōgun Ashikaga Yoshiteru is assassinated, and Oda Nobunaga installs Ashikaga Yoshiaki as his puppet
Oda Nobunaga drives Ashikaga Yoshiaki out of Kyoto, ending the shogunate

f.successor: Sengoku period; rule of Oda Nobunaga
